source.title: Mechanistic Tomography: Designed Measurement for Control-Oriented Interpretability

page_placements.theme: Named sources of compensation other than copy suppression, and how large they are

record.file_problem: None noted; the full paper text, including appendices, is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study uses a different measurement procedure to test conditional interactions involving GPT-2-small IOI Negative Name Movers, a narrow-task example of the copy-suppression role. It does not test L10H7 or the original training-distribution claim.
record.gate_note: The IOI group-ablation and held-out subset-prediction results are the study's own measurements and are recorded below. General discussion of copy suppression and results cited from prior work are not rows. The illustrative clean margin of 1.5 logits is explicitly hypothetical and is not recorded.
record.test_reason: The study runs its own group ablations of GPT-2-small IOI Negative Name Movers (10.7, 11.10) alone and jointly with primary Name Movers. Removing E raises the IO-vs-S margin by about 2.3 logits while primaries are intact and by much less once primaries are ablated. This bears on V5 (NNMs act as conditional copy suppressors) and on V4 (ablating the copier leaves less to suppress, which partly compensates). It uses a different method from the original's single-head L10H7 analysis.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely right. The authors conclude that in GPT-2-small IOI, Negative Name Movers act as conditional copy suppressors. P×E is the largest and most stable of three group-pair interactions, both in direct ablations and in held-out subset prediction. Conditional backup (P×B) is also reproduced. They make no claim about individual head pairs or a complete decomposition. The predictive comparison covers one template and mean ablation.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses designed group ablations and held-out prediction of subset interventions, rather than the original study's detailed single-head L10H7 circuit analysis and training-distribution measurements.
record.method_sensitivity: Direct interaction ordering is reported to persist across eight lexical/order conditions and both template-conditioned mean and zero ablation. The held-out predictive comparison uses one prompt template and mean ablation.

fits_no_version.finding: Conditional backup: P×B direct interaction of 1.080 (mean) and 1.268 (zero). This is smaller than P×E in every tested condition (contrast 0.750 / 0.413).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In IOI, compensation via reduced copy suppression exceeds compensation via backup Name Movers at the group level.

record.problems: The IOI evidence is group-level, not a test of individual head pairs. The predictive comparison uses one prompt template and mean ablation; the paper also reports a remaining three-way residual. The margin is not itself an emitted-token outcome.
record.rows_left_out: Other IOI pair-interaction rows not involving Negative Name Movers were omitted because they do not directly measure the copy-suppression role. The paper's other experiments concern measurement and observer methods outside the claim versions.

untested.parts: L10H7, training-distribution behaviour and the head's main role are not tested.
No QK/OV weight-circuit analysis and no loss-explained fraction.
Calibration is asserted from prior work, not measured.
Only group-level in IOI. The fraction of P's ablation effect that is compensated, and the distribution-wide case, are not quantified.
Individual NNM heads, other narrow tasks, and other models and sizes are not tested.
Distribution-wide sources of self-repair and LayerNorm rescaling are not measured.

missing.what: Δ(P+E) = −0.136 (mean) and −0.769 (zero), and Δ(P) ≈ 0.304. These are needed to compute E's conditional effect.
Direct B×E interaction: 0.502 [0.429, 0.576] mean, 0.518 [0.416, 0.618] zero. Positive, consistent with E suppressing backup-written names.
P×E remains largest under removal of any one lexical frame; normalized per pair it is 6.8× (mean) and 5.3× (zero) P×B. Three-way residual 0.319 / 0.601.

record.verdict_notes: Dropped the reader's limits_scope label. Group-level measurement and the one-template predictive study are untested scope, not qualifying results. The three-way residual does not contradict V5. r6 is a prediction-fit null, while the direct B×E interaction is positive. The study is not an original source. It repeats the original's calibration framing (V3) without testing it.

versions.untested_parts: The study does not test L10H7, token-level copying across the training distribution, or whether this is one head's main role.
No QK or OV weight-circuit analysis or 76.9% loss-effect estimate is reported.
The IOI margin measurements do not test calibration over the broader model distribution.
The study measures conditional interactions involving primary and negative name-mover groups, but does not test whether copy suppression compensates for ablation as a self-repair mechanism.
Tests the GPT-2-small IOI Negative Name Mover groups, not individual negative heads, other narrow tasks, or other models and sizes.
Does not estimate the distribution-wide contribution of copy suppression to self-repair or compare it with LayerNorm rescaling and other self-repair mechanisms.

rows.subject: GPT-2-small

rows.note: The paper describes this change as indistinguishable from no improvement; it is a comparison involving E, not evidence that all tested E interactions help prediction.
rows.check: A null predictive gain for a count-product term over the sampled subset masks cannot show whether E suppresses backup-written names. The direct B×E interaction in Table 3 is positive (0.502 mean, 0.518 zero) but is not recorded. Recording r6 as absent for V5 is misleading.

relationships.condition: GPT-2-small IOI, NNM group (10.7, 11.10), mean and zero ablation, eight lexical/order conditions
relationships.reason: Removing E boosts the copied IO name by about 2.3 logits (r1, r2), but much less after primary copiers are removed (I_PE 1.83/1.68, r3, r4). P×E also gives the largest held-out prediction gain (r5).
relationships.display_finding: Removing negative name movers raised the copied name by about 2.3 logits, with much smaller effects after primary copiers were removed and interaction estimates of 1.83 and 1.68, while the copier–suppressor interaction yielded the largest held-out prediction gain.

source_check.notes: All extracted values and conditions match the text. Evidence supports group-level IOI effects; predictive gains do not independently establish suppression, and neither individual-head mechanisms nor distribution-wide self-repair shares are established. Cross-study counts and rankings were outside this study-only check.

statements.correction: P×B interaction: 1.080 mean, 1.268 zero. P×E−P×B contrast: 0.750 mean, 0.413 zero. P×E exceeds P×B in every tested lexical/order condition. Authors rank three group interactions and explicitly disclaim a complete circuit decomposition; relative shares of self-repair are not quantified.
statements.problem: The interaction ordering is correct, but attributing a comparison of compensation amounts to the authors overstates their stated conclusion.
